stories.summary: OpenAI fired three researchers — Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak and Mikita Balesni — after an internal investigation found they violated policies on handling sensitive information, the company said in a post on X on Oct 9. The fired researchers published a letter arguing their dismissal could chill internal safety debates, with Balesni posting that they were 'fired for prioritizing safety'; OpenAI denied the firings were related to raising safety concerns.
stories.title: OpenAI fires three researchers over sensitive-information breach

stories.summary: The White House announced on Oct 8 that 11 tech companies committed a total of $2.4 billion in AI resources — which the administration dubs 'super intelligence' — to the Genesis Mission consortium of 15+ federal agencies working on energy, health and space. Nvidia led with $1 billion, followed by AMD ($500M), OpenAI ($200M), and Anthropic and Google ($150M each); Anthropic announced its pledge in a post on X, promising Claude access and technical support to federal agencies.
stories.title: Tech giants pledge $2.4B in AI resources to White House science mission

stories.summary: OpenAI began rolling out GPT-6 to free ChatGPT accounts on Oct 8 under the lighter 'Luna' variant, while paid plans get the stronger GPT-6 Sol; the rollout is gradual and global per OpenAI's release notes. The update also brings 'Intelligent UI,' letting ChatGPT answer with interactive charts, buttons, forms and small tools built directly into the chat, with 44% faster time-to-first-answer on search questions.
stories.title: GPT-6 Luna rolls out to free ChatGPT users with Intelligent UI

stories.summary: President Trump declared on Oct 8 that 'The White House considers anyone that uses the term, "Artificial Intelligence," as opposed to the highly accepted new and more accurate term, "Super Intelligence," THE ENEMY!' The statement escalates his Sept 29 executive order directing federal agencies to replace 'AI' with 'SI' in official communications — an order that carries no penalties and does not apply to private companies.
stories.title: Trump: anyone still saying 'artificial intelligence' is 'THE ENEMY'

stories.summary: USA Today Co (formerly Gannett) and its network of newspapers sued OpenAI in Manhattan federal court on Oct 8, alleging the company copied hundreds of thousands of their articles without permission to train ChatGPT. The 79-page complaint cites more than 160,000 entries from USA Today publications in OpenAI's WebText training dataset and seeks over $250 million in damages, an injunction, and the destruction of models containing their content; OpenAI has not commented.
stories.title: USA Today Co sues OpenAI for $250M over AI training copyright
